name: tccomp
description: tcsh filename completion works, asserted in the shape that the pending conversion of t_search's five name buffers to static would break (src/userland/tcsh/tw.parse.c -- 803 of a 926-byte frame, part of the shrink that takes tcsh from 133 pages of bank-0 stack to 74; written, measured, and DISABLED on the data bank -- see docs/history/audits/bank0-stack-status.md section 4).  t_search is the riskiest of the five conversions: it fills those buffers inside a loop over directory entries, so a static that were re-entered would corrupt a name mid-scan.  Typed one keystroke at a time through raw_inject because the interesting character is a TAB, which post_commands cannot deliver: 'ls /testda' + TAB + Enter.  /testda DOES NOT EXIST, so plain ls would fail -- a directory listing can only appear if completion filled in the rest.  Both halves are asserted: 'ls /testdata/' is the completed line echoed back (the completion itself), and 'colors.txt' is a file in that directory (the completed command actually ran).  Neither string is in the typed command, which is just 'tcsh'.
